name: Sundar Pichai

career.title: Product manager, later leading Google Toolbar, Chrome, ChromeOS and Google Drive
Senior Vice President overseeing Android, Chrome and Apps, then products broadly

background_rationale: Trained as a metallurgical engineer and materials scientist, he rose at Google as a product leader building Chrome and running Android before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: Reported that Alphabet's annual revenue exceeded $400 billion for the first time and guided 2026 capital spending to $175-185 billion, citing momentum after the Gemini 3 launch.
At Google I/O, said the Gemini app had passed 900 million monthly active users and introduced the Gemini 3.5 Flash model.
In Stanford's 2026 commencement address, described growing up in Chennai waiting years for a telephone and refrigerator and leaving his PhD program to get a job.
Raised Alphabet's 2026 capital-spending forecast to $195-205 billion from $180-190 billion to meet demand for AI infrastructure and cloud capacity; the stock fell about 7%.

personal_story.hook: Sundar Pichai's father spent a year's salary on his plane ticket to Stanford; he now runs Alphabet.
personal_story.summary: Pichai grew up in Chennai, India, the son of an electrical engineer and a stenographer, in a household where, he has said, the family waited years for a telephone, a TV and a refrigerator and worried whether water trucks would arrive during droughts. He studied metallurgical engineering at IIT Kharagpur and won a place at Stanford, where his father spent the equivalent of a year's salary on his ticket. He went to Stanford intending to earn a PhD and become an academic, but left the doctoral program because he needed to get a job sooner. After work at Applied Materials, a Wharton MBA and a stint at McKinsey, he joined Google as a product manager in 2004, led the creation of Chrome, and became Google's CEO in 2015 and Alphabet's in 2019.
